searchText: Should this EIP be pushed through the EIP process? https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1474 It has been stagnant for a while I believe. I think it will be updated soon and we can use it for the current process? Or you prefer to separate them? Or simply move the process into the stage at which is in Draft? https://github.com/ethereum-oasis/eth1.x-JSON-RPC-API-standard can we pin the OASIS link? I'm not a huge fan of doing a huge amount of rapid iteration of formalizing existing specifications in EIPs. I would *rather* see us start and iterate somewhere else that is a bit easier to iterate and then once it is all done use the EIP process to introduce changes going forward. Kind of like how the yellowpaper was the initial spec for Ethereum, and then changes went through the EIP process. We didn't try to spec out all of Ethereum in EIPs up front. Same with ETH2. I'd love it if *something* could be done about `debug_traceTransaction` and how ridiculous it can get in size...compression? idk but it's nearly impossible to trace some transactions because they're so large... Case in point: `0xd80a10106f2a8fb76cf6db6b9f7a64f08257b4952c94c888e1ac41ceb80733c9` will pretty much cause any Geth or Turbo-Geth instance to crash and burn. Nethermind has a timeout to protect it at least. But even Nethermind can't return debugs over 2GB. <@!372731338031366165> would pagination of responses help? Maybe? Geth and TG's rpcdaemon are killed by the OS from OOM before they even generate a reply If the reply was chunked and streamed back during processing to reduce the memory footprint, maybe, but that does nothing for the total size of the reply ah okay got it you can include the optional parameters that disable the stack and memory tracing What <@!489256758989029405> said, The bloat in debug transaction comes from the duplication of unchanged stack and memory across each VM invocation. Parity's format only puts the changes in each VM trace line, for example. hi <@!485238712415027221> 👋 hey folks Appreciate any input re: documenting the JSON-RPC API: https://github.com/ethereum-oasis/eth1.x-JSON-RPC-API-standard/issues/8 The short gist is: we've gotten a lot of feedback that the current eth.wiki page is suboptimal & my team (ethereum.org) is looking to help make improvements

excerpts.content:
I'd love it if *something* could be done about `debug_traceTransaction` and how ridiculous it can get in size...compression? idk but it's nearly impossible to trace some transactions because they're so large...

Case in point: `0xd80a10106f2a8fb76cf6db6b9f7a64f08257b4952c94c888e1ac41ceb80733c9` will pretty much cause any Geth or Turbo-Geth instance to crash and burn. Nethermind has a timeout to protect it at least. But even Nethermind can't return debugs over 2GB.
